flawed_step: Step 6: The inference that a cut containing at least half of all edges must be maximum is invalid.
counterexample: Let G be the 4-cycle with edges 12, 23, 34, 41. The partition {1,2}|{3,4} has cut value 2 and cannot be strictly improved by moving one vertex, but {1,3}|{2,4} has cut value 4.
assessment_summary:
1. Let (A,B) be a partition that cannot be strictly improved by moving one vertex. — Justified: this assumes exactly the hypothesis of the statement.
2. For each vertex v, let c(v) be its number of neighbors on the opposite side and s(v) its number of neighbors on the same side. — Justified: these quantities are well-defined in a finite simple graph.
3. Moving v changes the cut value by s(v)-c(v). — Justified: its same-side incident edges become crossing, while its crossing incident edges cease to cross.
4. Hence c(v) >= s(v) for every v. — Justified: otherwise moving v would strictly increase the cut value.
5. Summing over all vertices gives 2|C| >= 2|E\C|, so |C| >= |E|/2, where C is the set of crossing edges. — Justified: every crossing edge is counted twice among the c(v), and every noncrossing edge twice among the s(v).
6. Because every cut has value at most |E|, conclude that C is a maximum cut. — Not justified: the bounds |C| >= |E|/2 and OPT <= |E| do not imply |C|=OPT.
7. Consider the 4-cycle with edges 12, 23, 34, and 41. — Justified: this is a finite simple undirected unweighted graph covered by the definitions.
8. For the partition A={1,2}, B={3,4}, exactly edges 23 and 41 cross, so its cut value is 2. — Justified by direct inspection.
9. Every vertex has one crossing edge and one same-side edge, so moving any single vertex changes the cut value by 1-1=0. — Justified: no single-vertex move strictly improves this partition.
10. The partition A'={1,3}, B'={2,4} cuts all four edges and therefore has value 4. — Justified by direct inspection; 4 is also maximal because the graph has only four edges.
11. Thus the locally unimprovable cut of value 2 is not maximum, so the stated universal claim is false. — Justified by Steps 8–10.
